title: A localization map is regular
statement: Let $S$ be a commutative ring and $W\subseteq S$ a multiplicative subset, and let $\lambda:S\to S'$ be a localization of $S$ at $W$: (a) $\lambda(w)$ is a unit for every $w\in W$; (b) every element of $S'$ is $\lambda(s)\lambda(w)^{-1}$ with $s\in S$, $w\in W$; (c) $\lambda(s)=0$ implies $ws=0$ for some $w\in W$ (for instance $S'=W^{-1}S$ with $s\mapsto s/1$). Then $\lambda$ is a regular ring map [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. More precisely, for a prime $\mathfrak p\subset S$ with residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], the fibre ring $S'\otimes_S\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is isomorphic as a $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebra to $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ if $\mathfrak p\cap W=\emptyset$ and is the zero ring otherwise.

proof.text: Fix a prime $\mathfrak p\subset S$ and let $\psi:S\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)=S_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak p}$ be the canonical map [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change] (with $R=S$, $M=W$, $R'=S'$, $D=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ via $\psi$), the ring map $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_SS'$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, is a localization of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ at the multiplicative subset $\psi(W)$. Composing with the swap isomorphism $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_SS'\cong S'\otimes_S\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, $x\otimes s'\mapsto s'\otimes x$, the structure map $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to F:=S'\otimes_S\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, $x\mapsto1\otimes x$, of the fibre ring as a $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebra is a localization of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ at $\psi(W)$.

source.place: Section on localization (definition-localization, line 1069); written out by the agent

proof.text: If $\mathfrak p\cap W=\emptyset$, then by Step 3 every $\psi(w)$, $w\in W$, is a nonzero element of the field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, hence a unit, so by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-units-or-zero] (2) and Step 2 the structure map $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to F$ is an isomorphism of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebras. If some $w\in\mathfrak p\cap W$ exists, then $0=\psi(w)\in\psi(W)$ by Step 3, so $F$ is the zero ring by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-units-or-zero] (1) and Step 2. This proves the last assertion of the statement.

$F$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and geometrically regular over $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. Noetherian: by Step 4 $F$ is a field (ideals $0$ and $F$) or the zero ring (one ideal). Let $k'/k$ be a finite purely inseparable extension [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. If $F\cong k$ as $k$-algebras, then $k'\otimes_kF\cong k'\otimes_kk\cong k'$ ($a\otimes b\mapsto ab$), a field, hence a regular ring by [lem-weil-pbc-field-regular-ring] (regularity in the sense of [def-weil-regular-scheme] is invariant under ring isomorphisms). If $F=0$, then $k'\otimes_kF=0$, which is Noetherian and has no prime ideal (its only ideal is the whole ring), so the condition that every localization at a prime is a regular local ring holds vacuously and $0$ is a regular ring [def-weil-regular-scheme].
